item.title: “Immediate, Apocalyptic Freaking Out?”
item.description: This article summarizes and synthesizes the findings of several studies the authors conducted about school librarians 'perception of graphic novels. Censorship behaviors, both direct and indirect, are discussed, as well as the motivations for these actions, which include fear, external pressures, and discomfort and unfamiliarity with the format. Suggestions for creating a climate more conducive to students' right to read are offered.

item.title: In Step with Library Leaders: The Intersection Mindset
item.description: Wicked problems like climate change and health inequities demand cross-sector, interdisciplinary responses. This piece explores how libraries—often overlooked as agents of change—can become ecosystems for systemic transformation. By adopting an intersection mindset and embracing practices from high-impact nonprofits, libraries can catalyze collaboration, nurture adaptive thinking, and empower communities to act.
